74% of AI value is going to just 20% of companies.

This week, two major independent studies confirmed the same pattern. PwC measured that nearly three-quarters of AI's economic gains are concentrating in the top fifth of organizations. Separately, Deloitte surveyed 3,235 executives and found only 34% are genuinely reimagining their business with AI. Meanwhile, 37% are doing what most companies do — layering AI on top of workflows that have not changed in years.

Different research firms. Different methodologies. Identical conclusion.

The enterprise AI market is splitting into two groups. A small set of organizations is building compounding advantage — restructuring decisions, operations, and business models around AI. Everyone else is capturing efficiency gains that will become table stakes the moment competitors adopt the same tools.

The gap is not about technology access. Every company can subscribe to the same models. The gap is about leadership — whether AI is treated as a business architecture decision or an IT project.

By 2027, the efficiency gains from surface-level AI will be commoditized. The structural advantages will not.
